rationale: C23 plausibly supplied a concrete core of the later order. Its Labor Supply part assigns the Secretary of Labor substantially the same sequence of responsibilities later expanded in the child: assessing labor requirements and worker supply, formulating manpower plans, using the public employment system and labor-management cooperation, identifying critical occupations, and coordinating deferment policy with Defense and Selective Service. Several passages are nearly verbatim. C19 contains an earlier version of the same machinery, while C24 supplies the broader emergency-preparedness framework and reservation against implementing plans, but C23 is the closest material drafting template.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Periodically assess manpower resources... [and] analyze resource estimates in relation to estimated requirements
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Assemble and analyze Information on, and make a continuing appraisal of, the nation's labor requirements for defense and other activities and the supply of workers.
shared_material.explanation: Both direct the Secretary to continuously compare manpower supply with defense and civilian requirements.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Develop... plans, procedures and standards... [for] requirements for manpower
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Formulate plans, programs, and policies for meeting defense and essential civilian labor requirements.
shared_material.explanation: The child expands the same assigned planning function into detailed emergency procedures and standards.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Technical guidance to States for the utilization of the nationwide system of public employment offices
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Utilize the public employment service system, and enlist the cooperation and assistance of management and labor to carry out these plans and programs
shared_material.explanation: The child adapts the same public-employment-service machinery and labor-management participation.

shared_material.child_excerpt: Develop and maintain a list of critical occupations... With the Secretary of Defense, the Director of Selective Service System, and such other persons as the President may designate, the Secretary shall develop policies applicable to the deferment of registrants
shared_material.parent_excerpt: Determine the occupations critical to meeting the labor requirements of defense and essential civilian activities and with the Secretary of Defense, the Director of Selective Service, and such other persons as the Director of the Office of Defense Mobilization may designate develop policies applicable to the induction and deferment of personnel
shared_material.explanation: This is distinctive, nearly verbatim language assigning the same critical-occupation and deferment-policy mechanism to the same officials.
